scope: one attended native Finder AirDrop photo from the MacBook Air to a newly configured iPhone through Everyone mode
classification: anonymous control: sender and receiver were signed into different Apple accounts

sources: filtered macOS sharingd and Network.framework unified log
user confirmation of the anonymous accept UI and completed transfer
capture.packetCaptureReason: macOS denied access to the BPF device without elevated privileges

timeline.event: receiver did not support Hello; sender skipped it
native sender added preview data to the Ask request
Ask received HTTP 200 after user acceptance
sender extracted IDS session ID, pseudonym, and push token from the Ask response
Upload state started after Ask completed
sender selected CPIO with adaptive compression
Upload request object joined the established Ask HTTP messaging protocol
initial Upload request sent as HTTP/1 stream 2
adaptive compressor disabled compression for the incompressible photo

connectionTopology.policy: sequential Ask and Upload requests reuse one underlying TCP/TLS connection
connectionTopology.evidence: C82 joined http_messaging and used i29:c1:s2; C81 and C82 report the same flow UUID and local port, and no second TLS handshake was logged

ui.interpretation: Preview presence in Ask and preview rendering in the anonymous consent UI are independent; absence of a visible preview is not evidence of malformed file metadata.

confirmed: A native Mac can send to an unrelated iPhone through the Everyone route without a shared Apple-account identity.
The legacy protocol-0 receiver omitted Hello and the sender waited for Ask acceptance before starting Upload.
The native sender included preview data even though the anonymous iPhone accept prompt did not render a preview.
Ask and Upload were HTTP/1 streams 1 and 2 on one underlying TCP/TLS connection.
The successful photo used CPIO with adaptive compression, which switched compression off for the photo data.
notConfirmed: Encrypted request headers, binary plist bytes, and archive bytes were not recovered from the unified log.
The private IDS values returned by Ask were redacted.
The exact preview image format and dimensions were redacted.
This one receiver does not establish a universal topology for every AirDrop protocol version or direction.
implementationDecision: Use sequential Ask and Upload on the accepted TCP/TLS socket for espDrop's ESP-to-iPhone sender path; retain the fresh-Upload helper only as a directional research profile.
